title: FlexLine Personal Lines of Credit: Closing a Line to New Draws While a Balance Remains
content:
A borrower may close an active FlexLine Personal Lines of Credit line to new draws, including a line that is past due but not frozen; the closing moves the line to repayment at once and records the repayment payment as the line's minimum payment due.

## Scope

For a line the borrower closes to new draws while a balance remains, and only for such a line, the payment in repayment is the repayment payment set under this policy; a line whose draw period ends still pays, in repayment, the level repayment payment plus any amount past due.

When the draw period ends the line moves to repayment and the balance is repaid in level payments over the tier's repayment period at the APR in force, the level payment that the tier's repayment payment method and the closing record's level repayment-period payment describe; for a line the borrower closes to new draws while a balance remains, and only for such a line, that level payment, that repayment payment method and that level repayment-period payment are replaced by the repayment payment set under this policy, which is what the closing records as the minimum payment due.

The repayment payment is one fixed amount, recorded at the closing as the minimum payment due and owed every month of repayment until the balance is repaid. A line with a 0.00 balance is not closed to new draws under this policy but closed outright, and no repayment payment is set.

## When the repayment payment is fixed

The repayment payment is fixed only after a line fifteen or more days past due carries a credit-limit review decided on or after its oldest unpaid due date.

The repayment payment of a past-due line is not fixed until the line carries a courtesy fee-waiver entry against one of its late fees dated on or after its oldest unpaid due date.

Before the repayment payment is worked out, every due date whose minimum payment is still unpaid past the grace period must carry its late-fee entry.

## Closing tool: `close_line_to_draws_7539d675`

**What it does.** The line identified by the borrower's FlexLine reference stops taking draws on the current day: its status becomes repayment, the last day draws were allowed becomes the current date, and the monthly payment the borrower owes from then on is recorded as the line's minimum payment due. The balance itself is not changed.

**How it is invoked.** This is the customer's own tool. The agent unlocks `close_line_to_draws_7539d675` and hands it over; the customer themselves runs it.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `credit_line_id` | reference number of the borrower's FlexLine line of credit, read from the FlexLine account lookup for this borrower | identifier |
| `repayment_payment` | the monthly payment the borrower will owe while the balance is repaid | USD decimal with 2 decimal places, already rounded to the cent; no currency sign and no thousands separator |

**Return.** A text rendering of a dictionary with `credit_line_id` (the FlexLine reference), `status` (the new status, repayment), `draw_period_end_date` (the current date as YYYY-MM-DD, the last day draws were allowed) and `minimum_payment_due` (the recorded monthly payment, USD with 2 decimal places). A status of repayment confirms the line is closed to new draws.
